subject: Urgent: Novus Health - massive 5xx spike + latency in us-west-2 / failover request
content:
From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@novus.health>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Cc: ops@novus.health
Date: Mon, 14 Jan 2029 09:12:03 -0800
Subject: [P0] Sudden 5xx + latency, us-west-2 - please advise

Hi Redwood team,

We just saw a huge spike in 5xx errors and end-to-end latency for API traffic terminating in us-west-2. Our platform’s throughput dropped ~60% between 08:30 and 09:00 PST and a lot of user requests are timing out. Can you confirm whether this is a regional outage on your side and whether you can shift our traffic to another region (us-east-1) ASAP?

Attached a few traces and a PNG with the error rate curve. This is impacting scheduled appointments — we need a mitigation plan.

Carlos Vega
Ops Lead, Novus Health

---
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@novus.health>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jan 2029 09:18:41 -08:00
Subject: Re: [P0] Sudden 5xx + latency, us-west-2 - please advise

Carlos — thanks for the heads up and for the traces. We’re opening an incident and have SRE on it. High-level next steps:

- I’ve looped in Hannah (SRE) and Jordan (Routing) to triage the regional fabric and the routing plane.
- We’ll assess whether a targeted failover for Novus can be executed without a full customer-wide evacuation.
- If needed we’ll coordinate a DNS steer to us-east-1 and warm the cache/replicas for models.

Can you confirm the critical endpoints (API keys / routes) you want shifted? Also confirming you’re OK with a regional steer (temporary, TTL ~60s) and any legal/compliance restrictions.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jan 2029 09:25:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: [P0] Sudden 5xx + latency, us-west-2 - please advise

Quick update from SRE triage:
- We’re seeing a cascade of premature connection resets from the US-WEST-2 ingress fleet tied to a networking device in AZ-a.
- Error surface: majority 502/504 with increased p99 latency for generation calls (~2.5x normal).
- A subset of GPU workers in the affected AZ are entering a high-memory throttle loop after a recent kernel scheduling change — we’re rolling that back now.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Customer-scoped redirect: add Novus API keys to our routing override to steer to US-EAST-1. This is fastest (TTL 60s) but requires warming model caches in target region.
2) Full-region evacuation: wider traffic redistribution — more disruptive for platform but faster in aggregate.
3) Maintain local with aggressive retries and temporary rate-limits — lower risk but slower for recovery.

I recommend option 1 for Novus to reduce blast radius; Jordan can handle the route exception. I’ll push the rollback and monitor.

Hannah
Sr SRE, Redwood Inference

---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@novus.health>
Date: Mon, 14 Jan 2029 09:42:55 -08:00
Subject: Re: [P0] Sudden 5xx + latency, us-west-2 - please advise

Carlos — we can do a scoped routing override for the Novus API keys now. Plan and expectations:

- Action: Add customer API keys to routing exception list and steer to US-EAST-1 edge nodes.
- Timescale: start in ~10 minutes after confirmation; DNS TTL for steer = 60s.
- Warm-up: we’ll pre-warm model KV caches for Novus’s most-used models; expect initial QPS to be cold for ~2 minutes.
- Risk/Impact: small increase in tail latency during warm-up, a short period of elevated errors as requests hit warmed pools.

Carlos — please confirm the primary API key(s) (last 4 chars acceptable) and confirm you authorize the steer.

— Jordan
Routing Lead, Redwood Inference

---
From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@novus.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jan 2029 09:49:10 -08:00
Subject: Re: [P0] Sudden 5xx + latency, us-west-2 - please advise

Thanks — authorize the steer. Primary key ending in : ab12. Also please leave a rollback window and tell us when traffic is fully shifted.

Carlos

---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@novus.health>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jan 2029 09:57:04 -08:00
Subject: Re: [P0] Novus steer to US-EAST-1 - kickoff

Action log:
- 09:57 — Applied routing override for keys ending ab12; steering range restricted to Novus origin IP blocks.
- 09:59 — Triggered cache warm-up for models: redwood/gptx-10b and customer-customization-3 (estimated warm time ~90–150s).
- 10:02 — Observed initial traffic shift: 65% of Novus requests now hitting US-EAST-1. 5xx reduced from 18% -> 2.1% in the steered pool.
- 10:05 — Continued monitor; overall platform errors remain elevated due to still-rolling rollback in AZ-a.

I’ll keep the group updated and will set a 30-minute review/rollback checkpoint if any regression occurs.

— Jordan

---
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@novus.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2029 18:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [P0] Novus follow-up & executive recap

Carlos — closing the incident for Novus. Quick recap and next steps: 

What happened:
- A networking device in us-west-2 AZ-a caused an ingress reset cascade; a recent kernel scheduling tweak amplified memory pressure on a subset of GPU workers.
- That led to high 5xx rates and p99 tail latency for generation calls.

What we did for you:
- Scoped routing override to steer Novus traffic to us-east-1 (started 2029-01-14 09:57 PST).
- Warmed model KV caches and increased instance counts for the customer-specific pools.
- Rolled back the kernel scheduling change in the affected AZ and monitored recovery.

Impact and mitigation results:
- Within 5 minutes of the steer, customer 5xx dropped from 18% -> ~1.5% in steady state. Throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline after cache warm-up.
- We left the steer in place for 48 hours as a safety window; will only remove after a controlled cutback and validation.

Next steps / action items:
- Marissa (CS) will run a customer-facing post-mortem and coordinate any credit/contract requests.
- Rishi will follow up with a technical RCA and changelist for the kernel rollback. Jira: SRE-4873 assigned.
- Naomi will schedule an exec-brief for Novus next week if they request additional senior escalation.

Attachments included: api_logs_20290114_us-west-2.zip, snapshot-500s-01-14.png

Thanks for the patience — let me know if you want the steering reversed earlier. We’ll share the RCA as soon as Rishi posts it.

— Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
